policy_metadata.policy_title: Acupuncture for Chronic Lower Back Pain

sections.heading: Overview
content: This policy establishes Humana’s billing requirements and reimbursement guidelines, for 2022 and later, for the Medicare Part B benefit for acupuncture for chronic lower back pain (cLBP). Note: Some Humana Medicare Advantage (MA) plans have a supplemental benefit that covers acupuncture services that Original Medicare would not cover. This policy does not apply to services provided under one of those benefits.

sections.heading: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana MA plans cover dry needling and acupuncture services under the acupuncture for cLBP benefit for the same diagnoses as Original Medicare. Except where noted below, providers must report acupuncture for cLBP services consistent with guidance in applicable Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) published transmittals and Internet-only Manuals. Except where noted below, Humana MA plans allow acupuncture for cLBP services consistent with the applicable CMS guidance for the date of service.

subsections.heading: Practitioner Type
content: For dates of service on or after January 1, 2022, Humana MA plans’ acupuncture for cLBP benefit is not limited to services provided only by practitioner types that can provide services under Original Medicare’s acupuncture coverage. Instead, Humana MA plans permit practitioners who satisfy all applicable acupuncture licensure and plan requirements, such as plan participation requirements, to submit claims for services for acupuncture for cLBP.

subsections.heading: Number of Sessions
content: Humana treats all services covered under the acupuncture for cLBP benefit furnished the same day as if they were furnished in one session. For 2022 and later, Humana MA plans cover up to 20 sessions per year. Therefore, Humana MA plans do not require providers to report modifier KX for charges for acupuncture visits 13 through 20 in any calendar year, despite CMS acupuncture billing guidance, for Original Medicare, about modifier KX billing. Note: For 2022 through 2025, the 20-session limitation does not apply to services rendered by the patient’s primary care provider (PCP). For 2026, whether the 20-session limitation applies to services rendered by the patient’s PCP varies by plan as follows: • For Humana Group MA plans, the 20-session limitation does not apply to services rendered by the patient’s PCP. • For Humana Individual MA plans, the 20-session limitation does apply to services rendered by the patient’s PCP.
